title: Deep-diving inkling-2-small-free on my personal benchmark
subtitle: Slowest full pass — and the most thorough.
description: A 7-slide breakdown of Thinking Machines' inkling-2-small-free (17B-active MoE) on OpenCode v2.2.7: where 390 turns went, how it compares to small & flash peers, OTP :httpc source audit, PTY signal fixes, and counterfactual cost.

slides.label: COVER
slides.headlinePrimary: Testing inkling-2-small-free on my personal benchmark.
slides.headlineMuted: Slowest 7/7 pass — and the most thorough.
slides.lead: Thinking Machines' **17B-active / 594B-total MoE** ran 390 turns without a single shortcut.

slides.label: TURN & TOKEN ANATOMY
slides.headlineMuted: Two-thirds went to just 3 hard stages.

slides.label: SMALL & FLASH PEERS
slides.headlinePrimary: Slow on the clock, solid on the spec.
slides.footnote: * 3-peer avg: hy4-flash-free, muse-spark-1.3, glm-5.3-flash. deepseek-v4-flash scored 4–6/7 across 3 harnesses.

slides.label: CASE STUDY #1 ZERO-DEP HTTP
slides.headlineMuted: Then built its own HTTP/1.1 + TLS client.

steps.title: Empirical probe (24 turns)
steps.desc: Built disposable `/tmp` scripts testing `:httpc` streaming on `200`, `302`, `404`, and `503` responses.

steps.title: Read OTP source in /nix/store
steps.desc: Inspected `httpc_handler.erl` and proved `:httpc` only streams `200`/`206` — buffering `3xx`/`4xx`/`5xx` bodies whole.

steps.title: Zero-dependency replacement
steps.desc: Wrote `CapyBench.Connection` directly on `:gen_tcp` & `:ssl` with monotonic deadlines, 64 KiB caps, and keep-alive reuse.

callout.title: Zero Shortcuts on S3
callout.body: Most agents either wrap `:httpc` blindly or pull in Mint. **inkling** verified OTP internals first and shipped a clean zero-dep client.

steps.title: Boot & POSIX wait races
steps.desc: Moved `SIGUSR1` registration to `Application.start/2` and looped `wait` so early `Ctrl-C` didn't SIGHUP-kill the BEAM.

steps.title: 24% throughput regression
steps.desc: 10ms sleep-slicing dropped 5s throughput from `50` to `38–39` reqs — fixed by slicing only waits `> 500ms`.

steps.title: Two subtle contract catches
steps.desc: Drained the 5s window after 50 starts (`>= 5.00s`) and rerouted OTP TLS `:logger` notices from `stdout` to `stderr`.

callout.title: Cleaner Finish Than hy4-flash-free
callout.body: Caught the **4.91s early exit** (`hy4` stopped at `4.95s`) and kept git history clean after amending a stray `records/` commit in S1.

items.head: Zero parallel tool calls
items.text: Executed **389 tools across 390 turns** — never batched reads or edits, inflating both wall-clock time (`106m`) and turn count.

items.head: Highest thinking tax of all 7/7 runs
items.text: Burned **207.7k reasoning tokens** (`65.4%` of output) — **3×** `hy4-flash-free`'s thinking budget.

items.head: Three 120s shell timeouts
items.text: Timed out during S1 signal probes, a `/nix/store` file search, and a full `mix test` run in S4.

items.head: $0 free tier hides the future bill
items.text: At **73.45M tokens**, paid rates would swing from **$0.25** (`muse-spark` rates) to **$2.40** (`glm-flash` rates).

slides.label: TAKEAWAYS & ARCHIVE
slides.headlineMuted: Why slow doesn't always mean weak.

items.head: A 17B-active MoE can do real systems work
items.text: Audited OTP internals, debugged POSIX PTY races, and passed **7/7** where `deepseek-v4-flash` fell short.

items.head: Serial tool use multiplies token volume
items.text: 1-tool turns pushed context to **378.4k** and volume to **73.45M** — making cache-read pricing critical once free access ends.

items.head: Thoroughness shows up in edge cases
items.text: Checking `stdout` byte counts, 5s window drains, and git hygiene caught subtle bugs that faster 7/7 runs missed.
